title: New Citroën 2CV Will Go Full Retro, but with Electric Power

body_markdown:
Citroën will[reboot the emblematic 2CV](https://www.hagerty.com/media/news/2026-citroen-2cv-electric-official-debut-date-preview/) after years of rumors and at least one false start. The model is scheduled to make its public debut as a close-to-production concept on October 11, 2026, ahead of the Paris auto show. In the meantime, official preview images released by the French company give us a better idea of what the heritage-laced 2026 Citroën 2CV will look like.


Posted[on Instagram](https://www.instagram.com/citroen/) , the pictures confirm that the new 2CV borrows styling cues from several variants of the original car—and[there were many](https://www.hagerty.com/media/buying-and-selling/handy-citroen-2cv-buyers-guide/) . The 2CV’s basic silhouette remained pretty much unchanged between 1948 and 1990, but countless visual and mechanical details, including grilles, headlights, and engines, differentiate the older models from their newer counterparts.


On the new car, the headlights don’t fully stick out from the body (likely due to safety-related concerns), but they’re not totally flush, either. They’re rectangular like the ones that came standard on the 2CV during the 1970s. The rippled hood echoes[the early cars](https://www.hagerty.com/media/driving/citroen-2cv-seized-engine-roadtrip-story/) , and we even see a little bit of[the TPV](https://www.hagerty.com/media/automotive-history/the-mythical-very-small-car-that-birthed-frances-beloved-2cv/) (which spawned the 2CV) in the shape of the panel that’s below the windshield.


The door handles are surprisingly faithful to the original ones, and the turn signal repeaters are shaped like the ones Citroën fitted to the 2CV in the 1950s. The biggest difference is that, in on the 2026 concept, they’re repeaters. Seven decades ago, they *were* the turn signals.

An earlier preview image confirms that the shape of the next 2CV is old-school as well. The wheels are one of the only exceptions to the retro design that we’ve spotted so far: They have four lugs (the original came with steel wheels held on with three lugs).


The charming air-cooled flat-twin engine isn’t coming back. Instead, the latest 2CV will be electric. While official specifications aren’t available, front-wheel drive is nearly certain and a relatively small battery pack will likely come standard—it’s a city car, after all. It’s not too far-fetched to speculate a hybrid model will join the range at some point in the production run.


More details about the Citroën 2CV will emerge in the coming days, and a full debut will take place on October 11 at 7:00 p.m. Paris time, which is 1:00 p.m. in New York and 10:00 a.m. in California. Keep in mind that the car shown in Paris will be a concept, so what you see in the French capital won’t necessarily be exactly what we’ll get in showrooms. It should be close, though.
